errors: No real error. Gap: forgetting points of I or J̃ that are not in I' can make components unstable. The construction is therefore consistent only for 'special' (not necessarily stable) curves, or would need stabilization. The page does not discuss this.
Since S is kept while edges are removed, G' (and the resulting curve) can be disconnected. This is implicitly allowed but not commented on.

ideas.what: Partial normalization of a nodal curve along a chosen set of nodes, with the branch points over the unglued nodes becoming new marked points and an arbitrary subset I' ⊂ I ⊔ J̃ retained. This induces a map from G-pinned curves to G'-pinned curves, where G' is the graph with the same vertices, edges A' and legs I'.
ideas.modern_name: Boundary strata / clutching (gluing) morphisms of M̄_{g,n} and their inverses; graph contractions and leg-forgetting in the category of stable graphs (modular operad structure)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knudsen (1983) for clutching morphisms; Deligne–Mumford; Getzler–Kapranov (1998) and Behrend–Manin (1996) for the graph-categorical formalism
ideas.where_published: The general idea of the 'tour de Teichmüller' and gluing operations is in Esquisse d'un programme (1984). This specific formalization is unpublished as far as known.

ideas.what: Formula (126): the leg map I' → S induced by I → S and by the origin map Ã → S on half-edges.
ideas.modern_name: Half-edge formalism for graphs (flags with a vertex map and an involution)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine combinatorial bookkeeping of partial normalization and dual graphs. It is an early, careful half-edge formalism, but it is standard in the later literature (Knudsen, Getzler–Kapranov).
